recommendedTitle: Give the completion RPC one best-effort owner
summary: Five call sites invoke try_complete_campaign_if_drained and only two guard it. campaign-queue-completion.server.ts:51-68 and ivr/status.action.server.ts:130-153 catch and log; the #2048 campaign-settle-recheck.server.ts catches and logs under a third event name; campaign.server.ts continueOrCompleteDispatch and auto-dial.server.ts:437-444 do not catch at all, so an RPC failure propagates and fails the dispatch job or dial drain. An RPC failure only means 'not complete yet', which must never fail unrelated work.
currentBehavior: Completion failures are reported three different ways depending on surface, and on two surfaces they fail the surrounding job instead of being absorbed.
rootCause: Each call site invented its own try/catch and log message. The #2048 wrapper was created for the same reason, so there are now two wrappers and three policies.
resolution: One internal helper owns 'ask the gate, log, never throw', with a comment stating why. All five call sites use it and lose their own try/catch. Collapse campaign-settle-recheck.server.ts into the same owner rather than keeping two wrappers. Normalise the log event name and fields so a completion failure reads the same from every surface.

acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one code path owns the best-effort completion call

recommendedTitle: Prune stale non-production Twilio resources safely
summary: The dry-run report and both checks landed in PR #2733. scripts/twilio-resource-prune-report.mjs scans the parent account and every subaccount for TwiML Apps, Messaging Services, incoming phone numbers and subaccounts, and classifies each one with an environment check and an owner check. Only a resource named for a pull-request preview environment that no longer exists can be called stale; every other resource is KEEP or UNKNOWN. The report reads and prints and has no delete path. A first read-only run against the live account on 19 October 2026 found 771 stale TwiML Apps from closed pull-request previews, 5 protected resources and 270 resources whose owner could not be verified.
currentBehavior: Verified in PR #2733, 19 October 2026. 25 policy cases pass, and each safety check was broken on purpose to confirm the tests notice: a dead preview reported as KEEP fails 2, an unverifiable owner reported as STALE fails 2, dropping the workspace-number attachment check fails 1, dropping the ephemeral-preview requirement fails 1. A full read-only run against the live account exited 0 and scanned 1046 resources.
rootCause: Two separate gaps. First, the environment check had one source: the Railway CLI, which does not report pull-request preview environments at all, so the existing TwiML App prune script called every env:callcaster-pr-* app dead, including the app of a pull request that was open at that moment, and --apply would have deleted it. Second, there was no owner check at all: the Twilio account is shared by every environment, so a workspace missing from one database says nothing about its resources in another, and no tool applied that rule. Both are now explicit. The live set is the Railway environments plus one entry per open pull request, and it fails closed when either source cannot be read. A resource whose owner cannot be verified is UNKNOWN, never stale.
resolution: No source work remains. Run the report against each environment, act on the STALE list, and check the UNKNOWN entries against the environment that owns each one before deciding anything about them. The guard a delete path has to pass is written and tested in scripts/lib/twilio-resource-prune-policy.mjs, so a future delete path cannot skip the environment or owner check.
lookIn: scripts/lib/twilio-resource-prune-policy.mjs (the environment check, the owner check, the verdicts, the guard)
scripts/lib/live-environments.mjs (Railway environments plus one per open pull request)
scripts/lib/railway-environments.mjs (the Railway environment list, now shared)
scripts/local/prune-environment-twiml-apps.mjs (the existing delete path, now reading the same live set)
existingTests: test/twilio-resource-prune-policy.test.ts: 25 cases over the environment check, the owner check, the report counts and the delete guard
missingTests: No test drives the report script end to end against a stubbed Twilio client; the policy it depends on is covered, the wiring is checked by a live read-only run
The UNKNOWN resources are not resolved: each needs a check against the environment that owns it, which is an operational step
Subaccount deletion is not possible through the API; Twilio has no delete for a subaccount, so removal is a console action
acceptanceCriteria: A dry-run report lists the Twilio resources that may belong to a dead environment, and it changes nothing
Only an ephemeral pull-request preview environment can produce a stale verdict; production, dev, qa, visual-asset-review and staging never can
A workspace-owned resource whose owner cannot be verified is never reported as stale, because the Twilio account is shared by every environment
A pull-request preview is treated as alive while its pull request is open, and the tools fail closed when that cannot be determined
A delete path has to pass the environment check and the owner check, and the guard that enforces it is tested
trackerRecommendation: Lane is verify-close: the report and both checks landed in PR #2733, so do not rebuild them. What remains is operational: run the report, act on the STALE list, and check the UNKNOWN entries against the environment that owns them. Do not run --apply on the existing prune script until the live set is confirmed, because it deletes a TwiML App for good.

recommendedTitle: Release PRs must close the issues they promote (Closes #N)
summary: The gate shipped in PR #1960 was incomplete. It accepted a release body of `Closes #1, #2, #3` because its regex treated the comma list as a group of closing references. GitHub closes ONE issue per closing keyword, so only #1 closed. Release PR #2668 listed 17 issues that way and closed one: #2655 closed at the merge timestamp, #2663 and #2504 were closed by hand a day later, and #2605, #2503, #2513 and #2510 were never closed even though their fixes are in master. A sweep of the on-dev lane on 19 October 2026 found 57 open issues whose fix was already in production. The gate is now scripts/check-release-closing-references.mjs, which rejects the grouped form and names the numbers it would strand.
currentBehavior: Verified on dev@20f59d0e, 19 October 2026, in PR #2735. Twelve cases cover the real release 2668 body, a body that gives every issue its own keyword, a bare mention, prose that mentions a fix, a sentence after a keyword, a list whose later numbers have no hash, and the command line. Breaking the list detection fails five of the twelve. The dev-branch gate is untouched.
rootCause: The gate checked a shape GitHub does not honour. Its regex captured a comma list behind one keyword as a group of closing references, so the gate passed while GitHub ignored every number but the first.
resolution: No source work remains. The next dev to master release PR must write one keyword per issue; the gate names the numbers it would otherwise strand. The issues that shipped without closing have been closed and moved to on-prod.
lookIn: test/check-release-closing-references.test.ts (twelve cases, including the real release 2668 body)
existingTests: test/check-release-closing-references.test.ts: 12 cases over the grouped form, the correct form, prose false positives and the command line
acceptanceCriteria: A release PR body that names an issue behind a single closing keyword fails the gate
A release PR body that gives every issue its own keyword passes and closes them all
A bare mention and prose that mentions a fix are not treated as closing references
trackerRecommendation: Lane is verify-close: the gate shipped and the checker is tested. Do not rebuild it. The next release must use the correct body shape; the gate names what it would strand.
